words.gloss: even if it brings wealth or greatness

literal: Even if it brings wealth, deeds that are not honorable they will indeed not do, those who desire great fortitude along with honor.
translation: Those who desire great fortitude along with honor will never do deeds that are unworthy of their dignity, even if such deeds would bring them immense wealth or greatness.
modern: புகழுடன் கூடிய சிறந்த ஆண்மைத் தன்மையை விரும்புகின்றவர்கள், தமக்கு மிகுந்த செல்வம் தருவதாக இருந்தாலும், தமது பெருமைக்குத் தகாத செயல்களைச் செய்யவே மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the uncompromising nature of self-respect and honor. The poet explains that individuals who aspire to possess true strength of character and fortitude (pērāṇmai) alongside their honor (cīroṭu) will never stoop to doing things that are beneath their dignity (cīralla ceyyārē). Even if an action promises to bring them immense wealth, power, or external greatness (cīriṉum), they will reject it if it compromises their integrity. The word 'cīr' is used beautifully with different shades of meaning: first as material prosperity, then as fitting or honorable conduct, and finally as dignity itself. Thus, true honor is shown to be far more valuable than any material gain.
